Union Home Minister Amit Shah visited the Delhi Police headquarters on Jai Singh Marg in Central Delhi on Thursday (November 12, 2026) to review the law-and-order situation and policing in the national capital.
Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and other senior police officers were also present at the meeting. Shah arrived at the headquarters at 3.15 p.m. and left around 7 p.m.
The nearly four-hour-long meeting focused on the police force’s preparedness and the law-and-order situation in the Capital. However, the details of the discussions were not shared with the media, and senior police officers remained tight-lipped about the meeting. Sources said officers had also been instructed not to disclose its contents.
Less than a month ago, Mr. Shah had held a similar meeting with senior police officers, which was also attended by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta.
During the previous meeting, Mr. Shah reviewed the police’s preparedness to handle large gatherings and protests, intelligence gathering, crowd management and coordination among various units.
The discussions also covered women’s safety, drug trafficking, organised crime networks, traffic management and measures to prevent protests from escalating into law-and-order situations.
